C1.name: FRC.Interactions.tetrahedral_group
C1.doc: 27:C1, 27:C4 — `SU(2, 𝔽₃)` over `𝔽₉`: `24 = q(q² − 1)` elements, closed under the product, non-abelian, every trace `a + ā` in the shell, the orders `1, 2, 3, 4, 6` in multiplicities `1, 1, 8, 6, 8` (the binary tetrahedral group), the traces `0, 1, 2` in multiplicities `6, 9, 9`; the drive `diag(i, −i) = (i, 0)` lies in the group and its centraliser has `4` elements.

C1.name: FRC.Unitary.class_function
C1.doc: 27:C1, 27:C4 — the trace is a class function: `Tr (g M g⁻¹) = Tr M` for `g` of determinant one, `g⁻¹` the adjugate; in general `Tr (g M adj g) = det g · Tr M`. The Wilson trace of a plaquette is gauge-invariant.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.gauge_flux_invariant
C2.doc: 27:C2, 27:X1 — gauge invariance of the plaquette flux: with the corner gauges `φ₀, φ₁, φ₂, φ₃` and the links `A: 0 → 1`, `B: 1 → 2`, `C: 3 → 2`, `D: 0 → 3`, the transformed links `A + φ₁ − φ₀`, `B + φ₂ − φ₁`, `C + φ₂ − φ₃`, `D + φ₃ − φ₀` carry the flux `A + B − C − D` of the original.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.projector_forced
C2.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the photon's operator forced. A rotation-invariant quadratic symbol with constant part is `σ(k) = a k k + b |k|² δ + c δ`; gauge invariance, `σ(k) k = 0` for every `k`, reads `((a + b) |k|² + c) k = 0`, and its two evaluations at `|k|² = 1` and `|k|² = 2` give `a + b = 0` and `c = 0`: the symbol is `b (|k|² δ − k k)`, the transverse projector, massless (`c = 0`) and unique up to the one coefficient.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.admissible_two
C2.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the two admissible vectors satisfy every one of the `1 023` constraint rows (python's `13 338` rows distinct up to a scalar; that the range-1 translation-, gauge- and hypercubic-invariant quadratic actions at `L = 4` form exactly a two-dimensional space is the rank `121` of the rows, python's check A5), Maxwell's plaquette action satisfies them too, and it is their difference: `2 · Maxwell = B − A`.

C3.name: FRC.Interactions.green_torus
C3.doc: 27:C3 — the `L = 4` Coulomb Green's function in exact rationals: `7680 G` is the integer table, `ΔG = δ − 1/64` at every site (`7680 Δg = 7680 δ − 120`), `G(1, 0, 0) = 257/7680` (two unit charges at separation `1`), the table is cubic-symmetric on the axis and monotone `G(0) > G(1) > G(2)`, and its total is `0` (the zero mode removed).

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.drive_adjoint
C4.doc: 27:C4, 27:X1 — the drive `δ = diag(2, 7)` of `𝔽₁₃` (`δ⁻¹ = diag(7, 2)`): `Ad_δ H = H`, `Ad_δ E = 4 E`, `Ad_δ F = 10 F` with `4 · 10 ≡ 1`; the centraliser of `δ` in `SL₂(𝔽₁₃)` has `12` elements (the split torus); the non-split torus element `[[3, 4], [2, 3]]` (`a = 3, b = 2, ν = 2`, `a² − ν b² = 1`) does not commute with the drive.

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.va_cancel
C4.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the V − A cancellation: on a prime shell, for `u^N = 1` and `u^{2δ} ≠ 1`, `Σ_{τ<N} u^{2δτ} = 0` (the counter-aligned branch) while `Σ_{τ<N} 1 = N` (the aligned branch).

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.orientation_flip
C4.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the orientation convention `ε ↦ −ε` relabels the branches and leaves the selection: the inverse exponent `2(N − δ)` is as far from the identity as `2δ` (`u^{2δ} u^{2(N−δ)} = u^{2N} = 1`), so its branch sums to `0` too; the two conventions disagree on the label (`1 ≠ −1`) and agree that the coupled branch is the drive-aligned one (`ε · ε > 0` for both signs).

C4.name: FRC.Interactions.tetrahedral_group
C4.doc: 27:C1, 27:C4 — `SU(2, 𝔽₃)` over `𝔽₉`: `24 = q(q² − 1)` elements, closed under the product, non-abelian, every trace `a + ā` in the shell, the orders `1, 2, 3, 4, 6` in multiplicities `1, 1, 8, 6, 8` (the binary tetrahedral group), the traces `0, 1, 2` in multiplicities `6, 9, 9`; the drive `diag(i, −i) = (i, 0)` lies in the group and its centraliser has `4` elements.

C4.name: FRC.Unitary.class_function
C4.doc: 27:C1, 27:C4 — the trace is a class function: `Tr (g M g⁻¹) = Tr M` for `g` of determinant one, `g⁻¹` the adjugate; in general `Tr (g M adj g) = det g · Tr M`. The Wilson trace of a plaquette is gauge-invariant.

C5.name: FRC.Interactions.hessian_neutral
C5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X3, 27:X5 — the neutral Hessian, cleared of `¼`: with `m₀₀ = g² v²`, `m₀₁ = −g g′ v²`, `m₁₁ = g′² v²`, `m₀₀ m₁₁ − m₀₁² = 0` (the massless photon); `(m₀₀, m₀₁) · (g′, g) = 0` and `(m₀₁, m₁₁) · (g′, g) = 0`; the block applied to `(g, −g′)` returns `(g² + g′²) v² · (g, −g′)`.

C5.name: FRC.Interactions.hessian_full
C5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the full `4 × 4` Hessian of the gauged doublet on `𝔽₁₃` (`i = 5`, `g = 1`, `g′ = 2`, `v = 2`, `h = 7`) and on `𝔽₅` (`i = 2`, `g = g′ = 1`, `v = 2`, `h = 3`): `(0, 0, g′, g)` is the kernel (the photon), `det (W₃, B) = 0`, `W₁` and `W₂` are degenerate, the `(W₃, B)` trace is `M_Z² = (g² + g′²) v² h²`, and the custodial identity `M_W² (g² + g′²) = M_Z² g²` (`ρ = 1`) holds with `M_W² = M₁₁`; `i² = −1` and `2h = 1` on both shells.

C5.name: FRC.Interactions.five_eighths
C5.doc: 27:C5 — `M_W²/M_Z² = cos²θ_W = 5/8`: `M_W² = g² v²/4` and `M_Z² = (g² + g′²) v²/4`, so the ratio is `g²/(g² + g′²)`; where `sin²θ_W = g′²/(g² + g′²) = 3/8`, that is `8 g′² = 3 (g² + g′²)`, the ratio reads `8 g² = 5 (g² + g′²)`, on every shell.

C6.name: FRC.Interactions.weinberg_angle
C6.doc: 27:C6, 27:X4 — the Weinberg angle from the charge spectrum of one generation: over the sixteen states of `gen16`, `Σ (6T₃)² = 72` and `Σ (6Q)² = 192`, so `Tr T₃² = 2`, `Tr Q² = 16/3` and `sin²θ_W = Tr T₃²/Tr Q² = 72/192 = 3/8` (`72 · 8 = 192 · 3`).

C6.name: FRC.Interactions.one_generation
C6.doc: 00:G11, 27:C6, 27:C8, 27:X2, 27:X8, 27:P2, 27:P6, 27:P7 — one generation as the spinor `16` of the rank-five frame read `3 + 2`. The content by multiplet (colour indices, weak indices, `6Y`): `(0,0,0)`, `(2,0,−4)` ×3, `(1,1,1)` ×6, `(0,2,6)`, `(3,1,−3)` ×2, `(2,2,2)` ×3, that is `ν^c + u^c + Q + e^c + L + d^c`; the charges `6Q`; the anomaly sums `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, `SU(3)²Y = 0` (the colour triplets and antitriplets), `SU(2)²Y = 0` (the doublets); as many triplets as antitriplets; an even number of doublets (Witten); and the right-handed neutrino, the state `∅`, neutral and a singlet; the charges `6Q` of the list give the proton's `6Q(uud) = 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 = 6Q(e⁺)` (27:X2).

C7.name: FRC.Interactions.su3_centre
C7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7 — the scalar centre of `SU(3, 2)` over `𝔽₄`: the scalars `x I` with `x x̄ = 1` and `x³ = 1` are the three cube roots of unity `1, w, w²` (`ℤ₃`, colour triality), `0` is not one, and each commutes with `U₁` and `U₂`; that the centre is no larger is the ledger file's check E1 (all `216²` products).

C7.name: FRC.Interactions.gluon_commutator
C7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7, 27:X1 — the gluon self-coupling over `𝔽₄`: the two elements `U₁ = [[0,0,1],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]]` and `U₂ = [[0,0,1],[0,w,0],[w²,0,0]]` of `SU(3, 2)` (`U†U = I`, `det U = 1`) do not commute, their commutator plaquette `U₁U₂U₁⁻¹U₂⁻¹ = diag(w², 1, w) ≠ I`, while the abelian control `D₁ = diag(1, w, w²)`, `D₂ = diag(w, 1, w²)` returns `I`.

C7.name: FRC.Interactions.rank_tower
C7.doc: 27:C7, 27:X7 — the rank tower: for `Ω ≡ 5 (mod 12)` the cycle `Ω + 1 ≡ 6 (mod 12)` carries the ranks `1, 2, 3`, `2 ∣ Ω + 1` and `3 ∣ Ω + 1`, and stops there: `Ω + 1 ≡ 2 (mod 4)`, so `4 ∤ Ω + 1` and `gcd(4, Ω + 1) = 2`. The colour rank is `3`, the isospin rank `2`.

C9.name: FRC.Interactions.unification_counts
C9.doc: 27:C9 — the unification counts: `dim SU(5) − dim (SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)) = 24 − (8 + 3 + 1) = 12 = 2 · (3 · 2)`, the colour–isospin off-block; the spinor `16 = 1 + 5 + 10`; `dim SO(10) = 10 · 9 / 2 = 45`.

C9.name: FRC.Interactions.fifth_direction
C9.doc: 00:G12, 27:C9 — the quarter-turn as the fifth direction maps the sixteen `e_S` of four directions one-to-one onto the sixteen even subsets of five directions, the chiral spinor `16`; for `|S|` odd the image is the product `e_S e_4` with sign `+1`.

C9.name: FRC.Interactions.offblock_automorphism
C9.doc: 27:C9, 27:X8, 00:Z5 — each colour–isospin transposition is an automorphism of the reflection algebra of five directions up to the sign of the basis element: for all `S, T < 32`, `e_{τS} e_{τT}` vanishes exactly when `e_S e_T` does, and otherwise is `± e_{τ(S∪T)}`; the relabelling is a bijection of the `32` subsets.

C10.name: FRC.Ladder.tower_reduces
C10.doc: 26:G2, 27:C10, 27:X9, 27:P1 — a tower exponent is read modulo `n`: `g^{(g^j)} = g^{(g^j) mod n}`; tetration is exponentiation of a reduced index, and the two cyclic structures host every iterate (the ladder of the four roles closes: the fifth step returns to counting, 27-fields' C10).

C11.name: FRC.Interactions.residue_five
C11.doc: 27:C11 — `Ω ≡ 5 (mod 12)` is the conjunction `Ω ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `Ω ≡ 2 (mod 3)`, for every natural number: the twelve residues decide it, and the three moduli are periodic in `12`.

C11.name: FRC.Interactions.residue_instances
C11.doc: 27:C11 — the instances: the first eight admissible shells `5, 17, 29, 41, 53, 89, 101, 113` and the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561` (37-sim) read `5 (mod 12)`; the Koide carriers `13, 61, 157, 421` read `1 (mod 12)` and fail the criterion.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.gauge_flux_invariant
X1.doc: 27:C2, 27:X1 — gauge invariance of the plaquette flux: with the corner gauges `φ₀, φ₁, φ₂, φ₃` and the links `A: 0 → 1`, `B: 1 → 2`, `C: 3 → 2`, `D: 0 → 3`, the transformed links `A + φ₁ − φ₀`, `B + φ₂ − φ₁`, `C + φ₂ − φ₃`, `D + φ₃ − φ₀` carry the flux `A + B − C − D` of the original.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.drive_adjoint
X1.doc: 27:C4, 27:X1 — the drive `δ = diag(2, 7)` of `𝔽₁₃` (`δ⁻¹ = diag(7, 2)`): `Ad_δ H = H`, `Ad_δ E = 4 E`, `Ad_δ F = 10 F` with `4 · 10 ≡ 1`; the centraliser of `δ` in `SL₂(𝔽₁₃)` has `12` elements (the split torus); the non-split torus element `[[3, 4], [2, 3]]` (`a = 3, b = 2, ν = 2`, `a² − ν b² = 1`) does not commute with the drive.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.gluon_commutator

X2.name: FRC.Interactions.holonomy_stokes
X2.doc: 27:X2, 27:C2 — discrete Stokes on a `2 × 1` rectangle: the holonomy of the boundary loop, `A₁ + A₂ + B₃ − A₄ − A₅ − B₀` (two bottom links, the right link, two top links, the left link), equals the sum of the two enclosed plaquette fluxes `F₁ = A₁ + B₁ − A₅ − B₀` and `F₂ = A₂ + B₃ − A₄ − B₁`, the shared link `B₁` cancelling; the holonomy is additive over adjacent loops.

X3.name: FRC.Interactions.hessian_neutral
X3.doc: 27:C5, 27:X3, 27:X5 — the neutral Hessian, cleared of `¼`: with `m₀₀ = g² v²`, `m₀₁ = −g g′ v²`, `m₁₁ = g′² v²`, `m₀₀ m₁₁ − m₀₁² = 0` (the massless photon); `(m₀₀, m₀₁) · (g′, g) = 0` and `(m₀₁, m₁₁) · (g′, g) = 0`; the block applied to `(g, −g′)` returns `(g² + g′²) v² · (g, −g′)`.

X3.name: FRC.Interactions.projector_forced
X3.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the photon's operator forced. A rotation-invariant quadratic symbol with constant part is `σ(k) = a k k + b |k|² δ + c δ`; gauge invariance, `σ(k) k = 0` for every `k`, reads `((a + b) |k|² + c) k = 0`, and its two evaluations at `|k|² = 1` and `|k|² = 2` give `a + b = 0` and `c = 0`: the symbol is `b (|k|² δ − k k)`, the transverse projector, massless (`c = 0`) and unique up to the one coefficient.

X3.name: FRC.Interactions.admissible_two
X3.doc: 27:C2, 27:X3 — the two admissible vectors satisfy every one of the `1 023` constraint rows (python's `13 338` rows distinct up to a scalar; that the range-1 translation-, gauge- and hypercubic-invariant quadratic actions at `L = 4` form exactly a two-dimensional space is the rank `121` of the rows, python's check A5), Maxwell's plaquette action satisfies them too, and it is their difference: `2 · Maxwell = B − A`.

X4.name: FRC.Interactions.weinberg_angle
X4.doc: 27:C6, 27:X4 — the Weinberg angle from the charge spectrum of one generation: over the sixteen states of `gen16`, `Σ (6T₃)² = 72` and `Σ (6Q)² = 192`, so `Tr T₃² = 2`, `Tr Q² = 16/3` and `sin²θ_W = Tr T₃²/Tr Q² = 72/192 = 3/8` (`72 · 8 = 192 · 3`).

X5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X3, 27:X5 — the neutral Hessian, cleared of `¼`: with `m₀₀ = g² v²`, `m₀₁ = −g g′ v²`, `m₁₁ = g′² v²`, `m₀₀ m₁₁ − m₀₁² = 0` (the massless photon); `(m₀₀, m₀₁) · (g′, g) = 0` and `(m₀₁, m₁₁) · (g′, g) = 0`; the block applied to `(g, −g′)` returns `(g² + g′²) v² · (g, −g′)`.

X5.name: FRC.Interactions.hessian_full
X5.doc: 27:C5, 27:X5 — the full `4 × 4` Hessian of the gauged doublet on `𝔽₁₃` (`i = 5`, `g = 1`, `g′ = 2`, `v = 2`, `h = 7`) and on `𝔽₅` (`i = 2`, `g = g′ = 1`, `v = 2`, `h = 3`): `(0, 0, g′, g)` is the kernel (the photon), `det (W₃, B) = 0`, `W₁` and `W₂` are degenerate, the `(W₃, B)` trace is `M_Z² = (g² + g′²) v² h²`, and the custodial identity `M_W² (g² + g′²) = M_Z² g²` (`ρ = 1`) holds with `M_W² = M₁₁`; `i² = −1` and `2h = 1` on both shells.

X6.name: FRC.Interactions.va_cancel
X6.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the V − A cancellation: on a prime shell, for `u^N = 1` and `u^{2δ} ≠ 1`, `Σ_{τ<N} u^{2δτ} = 0` (the counter-aligned branch) while `Σ_{τ<N} 1 = N` (the aligned branch).

X6.name: FRC.Interactions.orientation_flip
X6.doc: 27:C4, 27:X6 — the orientation convention `ε ↦ −ε` relabels the branches and leaves the selection: the inverse exponent `2(N − δ)` is as far from the identity as `2δ` (`u^{2δ} u^{2(N−δ)} = u^{2N} = 1`), so its branch sums to `0` too; the two conventions disagree on the label (`1 ≠ −1`) and agree that the coupled branch is the drive-aligned one (`ε · ε > 0` for both signs).

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
X10.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_two_thirds
X10.doc: 00:G16, 28:C2, 27:X10, 27:P8 — `Q = 2/3 ⟺ ρ² = 1/2`: `3 Σ a_j² = 2 â₀²` exactly when `2 â₁ â₂ = â₀²`.

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
X10.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

X10.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_half
X10.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8 — the hypotheses of `koide_extension` hold on every frame `p = 4κ + 1`, the Carrier included: `h = 2κ + 1` has `h + h = 1`, and `ν = −3` has `ν + 3 = 0`.

X11.name: FRC.Unitary.hermitian_det_real
X11.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the determinant of a Hermitian `3 × 3` matrix over the extension is its own conjugate: `A† = A` gives `conj (det A) = det A`; its imaginary part is then `2`-torsion (`hermitian_det_shell`), so on every odd shell `det A` lies in the shell and `arg det A = 0`.

X11.name: FRC.Unitary.hermitian_det_shell
X11.doc: 27:X11, 27:P9, 00:G7 — the determinant of a Hermitian `3 × 3` matrix has `2`-torsion imaginary part: on every odd shell it lies in the shell.

X11.name: FRC.Interactions.ckm_free
X11.doc: 27:X11 — over `𝔽₁₇[√−3]` and `𝔽₅₃[√−3]`: the textured up and down mass matrices and the circulant are Hermitian (`M† = M` entrywise), their determinants are nonzero and lie in the shell with `det (M_u M_d)` (`arg det = 0`, the strong-CP angle vanishes), and `[M_u, M_d] ≠ 0` (no flavour symmetry forces the two to be simultaneously diagonal).
